item.title: Bulletin updated at 00:00 HKT 26/Oct/2024
item.author: hkowm@hko.gov.hk (Hong Kong Observatory)
item.description:
General Situation:
Tropical Cyclone Trami will move across the central and northern parts of the South China Sea towards the seas south of Hainan Island today. Meanwhile, the northeast monsoon will continue to affect southern China. Under the combined effect of the northeast monsoon and Trami, it will be windy with a few squally showers over the coast of southern China and the northern part of the South China Sea. There are uncertainties in the subsequent movement and intensity of Trami. It may linger over the seas south of Hainan Island early next week and even turn eastwards moving across the central and northern parts of the South China Sea again. However, Trami is expected to weaken by then and maintain quite some distance from the coast of Guangdong. Under the influence of an upper-air disturbance and Trami, there will be a few showers over the western coast of southern China. A dry replenishment of the northeast monsoon is expected to affect southern China midweek next week. It will be slightly cooler over the region in the morning and at night. Temperature difference between day and night will be relatively large.
